newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt bus workers end strike, police detain 33.
newsitem.headline: Egypt bus workers end strike, police detain 33.

text.p: More than 2,000 Egyptian public transport workers have gone back to work after two days on strike in protest at a decision not to give them an annual bonus, security sources said on Saturday.

Police in the Nile Delta province of Gharbiya have detained for questioning 33 people from among the 2,700 bus conductors, drivers and other transport workers who went on strike in the provincial capital Tanta, they added.
The strike paralysed work on Thursday and Friday in Tanta's textile mills, whose employees depend on buses to get to work.
On Thursday police said they arrested seven workers in Tanta and three in the nearby town of el-Mahalla el-Kobra who they thought were behind a one-day strike there.
Strikes are both illegal and rare in Egypt.

The protest began on Wednesday after the governor of Gharbiya cancelled the bonus of two months' salary which the workers have received every January for the past 15 years. He also decided not to issue them with new uniforms because the company had incurred losses last year.
Many workers also said they had not been given full-time contracts with the company despite many years of service.
The sources said the bus company did not respond to any of the workers' complaints.
